review.material: Primary scan: shape and label foundations, numerical-weight operations, weighted part relations, and the final coordinated-description example.
review.limitations: Selected definitions and examples were reviewed with OCR and visual checking of p. 416. Other property algebras are not assumed to behave identically to the numerical example.

evidence.description: Labels distinguish collections whose elements interact by matching labels.
Numerical order, maximum/minimum, truncated subtraction and geometric subdivision.
A row of cubes is related to plans, elevations and shaded-area descriptions.

sections.title: In brief
sections.text: Weights extends shape computation beyond bare geometry. Labels classify elements; weights let properties such as line thickness or tone participate in matching and combination.

sections.title: The question
sections.text: How should extra properties interact where shapes overlap, and how can several descriptions refer consistently to the same design?

sections.title: Main idea or claim
sections.text: Properties need algebraic rules of their own. Geometrically identical shapes may behave differently because their labels or weights differ; multiple descriptions can be coordinated through a grammar.

sections.title: How the work approaches it
sections.text: For numerical weights, the paper uses maximum for sum, minimum for product and subtraction clipped at zero for difference. Geometry is divided into overlap and non-overlap pieces before assigning the appropriate result weights.

sections.title: Evidence and examples
sections.text: Line-thickness and shaded-region examples explain the operations. The concluding cube-row construction coordinates plan, elevation and shaded-area descriptions, using labels and rules to maintain their relationship.

sections.title: What comes out of it
sections.text: Weighted part relations compare both geometry and property values. Coordinated grammars can change one description while requiring corresponding changes in others; geometry alone does not carry all the design information.

sections.title: Limits to keep in mind
sections.text: These weights are formal properties, not physical mass or a universal model of ink blending. Maximum-based addition does not mean arithmetic accumulation. The paper provides constructions rather than measured software or fabrication tests.

sections.title: What to take from it
sections.text: Before adding colour or thickness to a shape system, decide how values compare, combine and disappear. Merely drawing a different stroke width leaves the computational meaning unspecified.
